reason: The passage portrays Moses being divinely commissioned to lead the Israelites out of Egypt and to negotiate with Pharaoh for their liberation. God explicitly establishes him as the leader of a national effort, stating 'I have made you a god to Pharaoh' and commanding him to speak on behalf of the Israelite nation. While Moses initially hesitates and the people have not yet accepted him, he is unmistakably being positioned as the national leader through whom God will accomplish Israel's freedom and establish them as a nation. This constitutes portrayal as both an aspiring leader (accepting a divine calling to lead) and a nascent national leader (being actively commissioned for this role).
